question: What do we mean by 'posture' when talking about nursing practice?

options.A: The total weight of a patient during bed transfer
options.B: The alignment of body parts while holding a position
options.C: The muscular strength required to lift heavy equipment
options.D: The speed at which a nurse walks down the ward

explanation: Think of posture as how your head, trunk, arms, and legs line up whether you are standing, sitting, or lying down. You've got this! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h1)

question: Why is keeping good posture and body support so important for nurses on the ward?

options.A: It ensures patients recover faster from surgical procedures
options.B: It prevents physical strain and injury during patient care tasks
options.C: It eliminates the need for assistive lifting devices in wards
options.D: It speeds up the documentation process at the nursing station

explanation: Nursing is physical work! Maintaining proper posture protects your back and joints from everyday strain when you're helping patients move. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h1)

question: When an adult is standing normally, where is their center of gravity located?
explanation: Your center of balance (gravity) is right around your pelvic area. Knowing this helps you understand how we keep our balance! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h2)

question: How can you as a nurse make yourself more stable when lifting something heavy?

options.A: By widening the base of support between the feet
options.B: By bringing the feet close together to increase speed
options.C: By bending the upper back instead of the knees
options.D: By keeping the center of gravity high above the waist

explanation: Spreading your feet apart gives you a wider base, making you much more balanced and steady when lifting. Simple and effective! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h2)

question: What is a great health benefit of keeping your spine nicely aligned?

options.A: Full lung expansion and efficient gas exchange
options.B: Lower resting heart rate during sleep periods
options.C: Increased production of red blood cells in bone marrow
options.D: Faster clearance of medication through the kidneys

explanation: When you stand or sit tall, your chest isn't squished, letting your lungs fill up completely with every breath you take. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h3)

question: What happens inside a patient's body when they sit slumped over for a long time?

options.A: The thoracic and abdominal organs become compressed
options.B: Blood circulation to the brain increases significantly
options.C: The diaphragm gains extra strength from resistance
options.D: Digestive enzymes are secreted at a much faster rate

explanation: Slumping crowds your chest and tummy, squeezing your organs and making it harder for them to work comfortably. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h3)

question: Which nutrient is a must-have for keeping bones strong and healthy?
explanation: Calcium is the star nutrient for strong bones! It keeps your skeletal structure solid and healthy. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h4)

question: How does feeling really tired usually affect someone's posture?

options.A: It forces the spine into an over-corrected rigid extension
options.B: It has no noticeable impact on skeletal alignment
options.C: It stimulates the nervous system to widen the base of support
options.D: It causes muscle relaxation to fail, resulting in a slumped posture

explanation: When our supporting muscles get tired, they can't fight gravity as well, which naturally leads to slouching. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h4)

question: What do we call the condition where the upper back curves outward more than normal?
explanation: Kyphosis is that forward rounding of the upper back you often see in older adults. You're learning the clinical terms step by step! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h5)

question: Which spinal condition involves a sideways curve in the backbone?
explanation: Scoliosis means the spine curves sideways, sometimes looking like a 'C' or an 'S'. Great clinical knowledge to keep in mind! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h5)

question: What is the first thing you check when looking at a standing patient's body alignment?
explanation: A quick glance to see if the shoulders and hips are level gives you an instant clue about their spinal alignment. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h6)

question: You notice a patient has an unsteady walk and poor posture. What should you do next?

options.A: Discharge the patient immediately since mobility is adequate
options.B: Document normal findings and ignore the observation
options.C: Implement fall prevention protocols and assess assistive device needs
options.D: Instruct the patient to run across the ward to test endurance

explanation: Unsteady walks mean a higher risk of falls. Keeping our patients safe is our top priority, so we put fall precautions in place right away! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h6)

question: What is the golden rule of body mechanics when lifting a heavy item from the floor?

options.A: Twist the torso quickly to build momentum
options.B: Bend at the knees and keep the back straight
options.C: Hold the heavy object far away from your chest
options.D: Keep the knees locked and bend at the waist

explanation: Always bend your knees, not your back! Let your strong leg muscles do the heavy lifting to protect your spine. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h7)

question: Why is it dangerous to twist your spine while lifting something heavy?

options.A: It cuts off blood circulation to the lower extremities
options.B: It places excessive shear stress on the intervertebral discs
options.C: It causes the center of gravity to drop below the feet
options.D: It instantly doubles the total body weight of the patient

explanation: Twisting under pressure forces your spinal discs in awkward directions, which is a fast track to muscle sprains or disk injury. Lift straight, turn with your feet instead! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h7)

question: Which bedside item is used specifically to prevent foot drop in a patient who has to stay in bed?
explanation: A footboard props the feet in a natural upright position, keeping tight calf muscles from pulling the feet downward into foot drop. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h8)

question: What is the main reason for placing a trochanter roll alongside a patient's thighs?

options.A: To support the arms during meal times
options.B: To prevent external rotation of the hips
options.C: To keep the heels elevated off the mattress
options.D: To prevent the patient from sitting up too fast

explanation: Trochanter rolls act like gentle bumpers that keep the patient's legs from rolling outward, maintaining nice, neutral leg alignment. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h8)
